title: incident-bot: actionable diagnostics quicklinks for on-call runbooks
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Add actionable quicklinks to incident-bot's diagnostics cards to speed access to runbooks for on-call responders. Feature gated behind `enable_quicklinks`.
description:
Motivation: On-call responders need faster access to the most relevant runbooks and remediation steps when incident-bot surfaces diagnostics. This change adds an actionable quicklinks layer to diagnostics cards so users can jump directly to runbooks, filtered by SLO and service context.

What: - New quicklink renderer that attaches 0..N prioritized runbook links to diagnostics suggestions. - Scoring heuristics that prefer runbooks matching SLO tags, service, and recent incident history. - Fallbacks that show runbook search when no exact match exists. - Small UI card update to show link icons and copy-to-clipboard. - Mapping YAML and unit tests for runbook metadata ingestion.

Checklist:
- [x] Design reviewed with SRE (Sanjay Rao)
- [x] Security review for open links and CSP fallback (Dana Liu)
- [x] Unit and integration tests added
- [x] Docs updated with how to add runbooks + mapping format
- [x] Feature gated behind `enable_quicklinks` flag for staged rollout

Notes: the implementation is feature-gated and does not change existing diagnostics behavior when disabled. Runbook mapping is pluggable and lives in pkg/slo/toolkit/mapping.yaml; we include a minimal default mapping to bootstrap. Related: ENG-5321 for design, SUP-4421 for customer report requesting faster runbook access.

summary_of_changes: Introduce actionable quicklinks for diagnostics: scoring, rendering, mapping ingestion, tests, docs, and gated rollout.
discussion: Alex Kim (reviewer): Can we ensure link generation is safe for on-prem deployments? We shouldn't leak internal URLs when running with private installer.

Maya Patel (author): Good catch. The quicklink generator uses runbook metadata from mapping.yaml; for private deployments we expect mappings to use internal URLs. We added a safety check that disables external URL generation when `private_deployment=true`. Added unit test.

Sanjay Rao (reviewer): Scoring looks biased towards SLO tag matches which is fine, but we should add a recency factor for runbooks used in recent incidents. Otherwise older but high-score runbooks may surface.
Maya Patel (author): Added a lightweight recency boost based on last_execution_ts (optional field). We cap the boost so it doesn't drown other signals. See quicklinks.go:scoreRunbook().
Dana Liu (security): Confirmed CSP and link target defaults. Also flagged that copy-to-clipboard needs user gesture; verified behavior on Chrome/Firefox.
Alex Kim (reviewer): lint failed on first CI run (formatting in quicklinks.go). Please run `gofmt` and re-run tests.
Maya Patel (author): Fixed formatting, addressed a nil-map panic for empty mappings, re-ran CI. Tests now pass.

Sanjay Rao: Approved.
Alex Kim: Approved.
ci_checks: integration-tests: pass (one flaky_test skipped with marker)
merge_outcome: Merged via squash and merge by Maya Patel (merge commit replaced with single squashed commit).
notes_for_ops: Rollout plan: enable behind feature flag, enable for 10% of orgs for 48h, monitor oncall.quicklinks.click_rate and oncall.quicklinks.misfires for regressions. If CSP issues appear, roll back the flag.
